scenes.visual: Title card 'Divided, Not Grown' over a single large pale-cream sphere (the egg). COLOUR MAP (both films): egg cytoplasm pale cream; inherited material (determinant) PURPLE dots; signals between cells GREEN arrows; ectoderm BLUE, mesoderm RED, endoderm YELLOW; calcium wave bright white-cyan. All numbers appear only as on-screen text.

scenes.tts: A frog egg divides into thousands of cells without growing at all. So where do the cells come from, and what does each one get?
scenes.visual: One large cream sphere labelled 'frog egg: one cell'. A fast-forward ghost shows it becoming a ball of many cells with the SAME outer outline; on-screen counter '1 cell → thousands of cells', and a dashed circle of the original outline stays exactly on top, label 'no growth'. Then it rewinds to one cell, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: A frog egg divides into thousands of cells without growing at all. So where do the cells come from, and what does each one get?

scenes.tts: Development starts at fertilization. A sperm fuses with the egg, and a wave of calcium crosses it. A frog egg was paused partway through meiosis, and the calcium wakes it. Only one sperm should get in, and the egg keeps the rest out.
scenes.visual: A small sperm cartoon reaches the sphere and merges at one point. A bright white-cyan ring spreads from that point across the whole egg (label 'calcium wave'). A label 'frog egg: paused in meiosis' changes to 'restarted'. Two more sperm reach the surface but stay outside and never enter (no bouncing, no repulsion shown); label 'extra sperm kept out'.
scenes.narration: Development starts at fertilization. A sperm fuses with the egg, and a wave of calcium crosses it. A frog egg was paused partway through meiosis, and the calcium wakes it. Only one sperm should get in, and the egg keeps the rest out.

scenes.tts: Next comes cleavage, a run of divisions with no growth between them. Each new cell is called a blastomere. One cell becomes two, then four, then eight.
scenes.visual: Furrows cut the sphere: 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 cells, each step animated as a pinching line. The outer outline stays fixed. One cell is tagged 'blastomere'. Counter at top: 'cells: 1, 2, 4, 8'.
scenes.narration: Next comes cleavage, a run of divisions with no growth between them. Each new cell is called a blastomere. One cell becomes two, then four, then eight.

scenes.tts: Watch the outline. It never gets bigger. Each division cuts the same egg into more, smaller pieces. The egg is divided, not grown.
scenes.visual: The dashed outline of the original egg pulses; the cells continue to 16 then 32 inside it. A size bar beside the embryo shows one cell's diameter shrinking at each step. Caption 'divided, not grown'.
scenes.narration: Watch the outline. It never gets bigger. Each division cuts the same egg into more, smaller pieces. The egg is divided, not grown.

scenes.tts: Suppose every division is equal. After five divisions there are thirty-two cells. Is each cell one thirty-second as wide as the egg?
scenes.visual: On screen: 'model: 5 equal divisions → 32 cells'. Beside the egg, a ruler shows the egg's width; a tiny dashed sphere labelled '1/32 of the width?' sits next to it. Question card: 'Is each cell 1/32 as wide?'
scenes.narration: Suppose every division is equal. After five divisions there are thirty-two cells. Is each cell one thirty-second as wide as the egg?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Question card holds; 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: No. In this equal model, each cell holds one thirty-second of the volume. But volume is shared out in three dimensions: length, width and depth. So each cell is about a third as wide as the egg.
scenes.visual: The tiny dashed sphere is replaced by a real blastomere drawn to scale beside the egg (computed: egg 124 µm, blastomere 39 µm for a 1 nL model egg; diameter ratio 3.17). On-screen text: 'volume ÷ 32', 'width ÷ 32^(1/3) ≈ 3.17'. No sub-cube array: only the two spheres at the true 3.17 diameter ratio.
scenes.narration: No. In this equal model, each cell holds one thirty-second of the volume. But volume is shared out in three dimensions: length, width and depth. So each cell is about a third as wide as the egg.

scenes.tts: Something else has changed. There are now thirty-two nuclei, but no new cytoplasm. Each nucleus has far less cytoplasm around it.
scenes.visual: Inside the 32-cell embryo every cell gets a dark nucleus dot. Counter panel: 'nuclei: 1 → 32' and 'cytoplasm: unchanged' with a flat bar.
scenes.narration: Something else has changed. There are now thirty-two nuclei, but no new cytoplasm. Each nucleus has far less cytoplasm around it.

scenes.tts: Now suppose the egg is not the same all through. Mark one region in purple. This stands for inherited material, placed in the egg before it divides.
scenes.visual: Rewind to the one-cell egg. A patch of PURPLE dots fills one side region. On-screen label: 'drawn in purple: inherited material'.
scenes.narration: Now suppose the egg is not the same all through. Mark one region in purple. This stands for inherited material, placed in the egg before it divides.

scenes.tts: Suppose the purple is anchored, so it stays put. The furrows cut through the egg around it. After a few divisions, only some cells hold it. Their neighbours have none.
scenes.visual: Small on-screen tag 'model: purple anchored, does not drift'. Cleavage replays 1 → 2 → 4 → 8 → 32 with the PURPLE dots staying in place; furrows slice through. At 32 cells, the cells containing purple get a bold outline; the rest are plain cream (schematic geometry; no count shown).
scenes.narration: Suppose the purple is anchored, so it stays put. The furrows cut through the egg around it. After a few divisions, only some cells hold it. Their neighbours have none.

scenes.tts: That is what a cell inherits: the slice of egg it was cut from. If an anchored molecule helps set fate, it is a cytoplasmic determinant.
scenes.visual: Zoom on one outlined purple cell and one plain neighbour side by side. Label over the purple cell: 'inherits'. Caption: 'cytoplasmic determinant: a localized molecule that helps set cell fate'.
scenes.narration: That is what a cell inherits: the slice of egg it was cut from. If an anchored molecule helps set fate, it is a cytoplasmic determinant.

scenes.tts: Yolk changes the cutting. Yolk is stored food, and it slows the furrows. A frog egg divides completely, with bigger cells in its yolky half. A chick divides only a disc on top of its yolk. A fly first divides its nuclei in shared cytoplasm, with no membranes between them.
scenes.visual: Side panel of three schematic eggs. Frog: whole egg divided, small cells on top, large yolky cells below. Chick: a big undivided yolk with a small divided disc on top. Fly: an elongated egg with many nuclei dots in shared cytoplasm and no cell membranes between them, then membranes form around the nuclei at the surface. Yolk shaded pale tan in all three.
scenes.narration: Yolk changes the cutting. Yolk is stored food, and it slows the furrows. A frog egg divides completely, with bigger cells in its yolky half. A chick divides only a disc on top of its yolk. A fly first divides its nuclei in shared cytoplasm, with no membranes between them.

scenes.tts: Edwin Conklin watched the egg of a sea squirt. Part of its cytoplasm is yellow, and it gathers into a crescent. He followed it cell by cell. It ended up mainly in the cells that build the larva's tail muscle.
scenes.visual: Caption 'Edwin Conklin, 1905; sea squirt (Styela)'. An egg with a crescent, drawn PURPLE, label 'yellow crescent, drawn in purple: inherited material'. Cleavage proceeds; the crescent cells keep their outline; jump to a tadpole-shaped larva whose tail muscle band is outlined, linked by a dotted line back to the crescent cells.
scenes.narration: Edwin Conklin watched the egg of a sea squirt. Part of its cytoplasm is yellow, and it gathers into a crescent. He followed it cell by cell. It ended up mainly in the cells that build the larva's tail muscle.

scenes.tts: But following a colour shows where it goes, not what it does. Does the crescent make muscle, or just ride along? That takes a different test.
scenes.visual: The larva fades. Two cartoon panels: 'where it goes' (dotted path, ticked) and 'what it does' (question mark, unticked). Caption: 'a fate map is not a cause'.
scenes.narration: But following a colour shows where it goes, not what it does. Does the crescent make muscle, or just ride along? That takes a different test.

scenes.tts: So cleavage shares out one fixed egg. Each cell gets its own slice, and anchored material comes with it.
scenes.visual: Final recap: the one-cell egg with its purple patch splits into the 32-cell embryo inside the fixed dashed outline; purple cells outlined.
scenes.narration: So cleavage shares out one fixed egg. Each cell gets its own slice, and anchored material comes with it.

scenes.visual: End card (Hex card) with one line only: 'The egg is divided, not grown: each cell inherits its own slice.'
